thread:
customer_jones: We're getting JSON parse errors in structured mode for payloads with backslashes followed by spaces in user addresses. Started after the last SDK update. Example below. Also seeing billing spikes from automatic retries.

Sara_support: hi @customer_jones — sorry about this. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl + body) and the exact error you see?

customer_jones: ```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"mode":"json","input":{"address":"C:\\ Reports\\ 2026\\Final"}}'
```
Error returned: `Invalid JSON: unexpected token '\' at position 74`

sara_support: thanks. assigning to eng, tagging @matt_engineer and @ingrid_oncall. We're going to reproduce.

matt_engineer: I can repro locally with `streaming=true` and small chunk sizes. When the chunk boundary splits a backslash and following whitespace we emit an incomplete escape sequence in the stream -> downstream parser fails. Quick log: 

```
chunk 1: ..."address":"C:\\\nchunk 2:  Reports\\ 2026\\Final"}...
parser sees: "C:\\\  Reports..." -> invalid escape
```

ingrid_oncall: looks like the stream-splitter treats `\ ` (backslash+space) as start of an escape and drops the continuation across chunk boundary. Workaround: set `stream=false` or use `escape_mode=full` for now. We'll prepare a patch.

matt_engineer: patch: stream-chunker preserves trailing backslashes across chunk boundaries and marks them as literal if followed by whitespace/newline. Added unit + integration tests. Rolling canary.

deploy-bot: canary rollout: prod-stream-chunker v1.3.3-canary -> 3 hosts

sara_support: pushed the temporary account config for you, @customer_jones. Can you re-run the same curl?

customer_jones: re-tested just now — request succeeded, no parse error, retries stopped and billing spike reversed. Thanks :tada:

matt_engineer: will roll to full prod in 2h unless any regressions reported. closing thread pending final observability checks.
